A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same local-protein representation framework, renamed from AFMs to MLFFs in v3. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, pKa and chemical-shift benchmarks, simulation-based analyses and descriptor-inversion results, including Tables B.1–B.4 and Appendix I.1.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds experimental-pKa comparisons, radius/layer ablations and descriptor-guided AlphaFold3 generation results.

M1.justification: V1 inverts descriptors by optimizing coordinates of an existing structure. V3 retains this procedure and adds descriptor-gradient guidance inside AlphaFold3 reverse diffusion from Gaussian noise, using a new zeroth-order descriptor objective (Appendix J.2.2). This substantially extends inference capabilities; the core local-descriptor and GCN framework remains.

E1.justification: V3 adds experimental-pKa evaluation using PKAD-R and crystallographic structures from PropKa's training cases, extending v1's evaluation against simulated PypKa targets. It also evaluates descriptor-conditioned generation from noise beyond the existing coordinate-inversion task. The original RefDB classification and chemical-shift coverage remains.

E2.justification: V3 adds ESM3 sequence/structure, ISM and ESMFold comparisons to classification, pKa and backbone chemical-shift experiments. Learned embeddings are added for pKa and backbone shifts, and Egret joins the pKa comparison. Conversely, the five side-chain ESM comparisons in v1 Table B.4 disappear from v3 Table B.6. V1's retained ESM comparator is identified as ESM2 in v3.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate all PKAD-R entries and PropKa training cases, vary environment radii and descriptor layers, and compare guided/unguided generation using signed normalized distance. The original 823/225 RefDB split and training budgets remain. Appendix F.2 reports concatenated MACE layers rather than v1's final-layer setting, although v3 retains conflicting final-layer wording; this does not establish that original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds radius and layer ablations (Tables B.9–B.10), descriptor-distance versus structural-RMSD analysis (Fig. A.10), and inversion/guidance studies on four additional proteins. The original atom-set ablations and chemical-shift case studies remain. The paired relaxed-minus-unrelaxed likelihood distribution shown in v1 Fig. 5 is removed.

E5.justification: V3 adds Pearson and Spearman correlation estimation for descriptor distances versus structural RMSD (Fig. A.10), supplementing v1's qualitative PCA analysis. Existing chemical-shift quantile bands and likelihood-based confidence reporting remain unchanged. Neither version specifies training seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark and atom-set ablation values remain unchanged; for example, MACE CA chemical-shift MAE remains 0.584 ppm. V3 adds extensive comparator, ablation and inversion results. Its new experimental-pKa comparison reports lysine MAE of 0.360 for MACE versus 0.648 for pKa-ANI, but histidine MAE of 0.925 versus 0.899 (Table B.8). Five side-chain ESM results and the paired-likelihood distribution are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix J.2.2 adds a guided reverse-diffusion equation, a piecewise descriptor objective (Eq. 14) and a signed normalized conformer-distance definition (Eq. 15). The existing KDE, feature-construction, GCN and direct-inversion mathematics remains substantially unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V3 explicitly claims generalization to rare chemistries and out-of-distribution conformations and describes uncertainty as calibrated in the Introduction. These specific assertions extend v1's claims about transferable local representations and useful confidence scores. The central representation, likelihood and chemical-shift contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies pKa comparisons by the mismatch between simulated and experimental supervision and by baseline training-set reuse, and attributes weaker histidine transfer to scarce training examples. It adds explanations for the radius/layer choices and interprets descriptor–RMSD correlations as approximate isometry (Appendices F, G.2 and J.1). Existing HA-prediction and side-chain reconstruction limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 provides a repository location and states that code, trained models and processing scripts are public (Section 10), information absent from v1. It adds learned-baseline input construction, descriptor-layer/API details, altloc residue ranges and diffusion guidance parameters of eta = 0.5 and delta = 0.25. Existing GCN hyperparameters and hardware descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds literature on ESM3, structural distillation, experimental-pKa data and score-based generation. It also changes its characterization of pKa-ANI from a related AFM representation method to fixed symmetry-function descriptors, sharpening the novelty contrast with contextual MLFF features. The broader positioning against small-molecule descriptor applications remains.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, background and discussion around MLFF representation reuse and transfer learning. It merges related work into the background, moves existing case studies into appendices, adds an experimental overview and reproducibility statement, and changes terminology, title, author information and citation style throughout.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to explain pretraining and transfer learning. Existing UMAP and ring-PCA figures move into the main text; comparison tables expand, and the chemical-shift table splits into backbone and side-chain tables. V3 adds overview, ablation and experimental-pKa tables plus correlation/guidance figures, removes the paired-likelihood panel and adopts conference formatting.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens validation: broader ESM/learned controls and experimental-pKa tests address v1's limited comparisons and reliance on simulated pKa references. Radius/layer ablations and expanded inversion studies make important design and transfer claims more assessable, while new access information improves reproducibility. Training-set-based pKa comparisons, unresolved reporting inconsistencies and dropped side-chain ESM results limit the gains, but the added evidence provides a clear, substantial net improvement.
